item.title: China announces measures to steady stock market
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
BEIJING, Nov. 22 (Xinhua) -- China will roll out a slew of measures to steady the stock market, including lowering the minimum margin requirement for leveraged stock purchases to generate incremental funds, the country's securities regulator said Sunday.
With approval from the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), the Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing stock exchanges will lower the minimum margin ratio from 100 percent to 80 percent, effective from Nov. 30, according to the CSRC.
The adjustment is estimated to theoretically bring in nearly 400 billion yuan (about 59.58 billion U.S. dollars) in incremental funds.
Adjustments to the ratio are seen as one of the key tools for conducting counter-cyclical regulation on China's stock market. Previous downward adjustments in history have increased margin balances and trading activity, playing a notable role in supporting the market, experts said.
The Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges also introduced a new batch of fee reduction measures, including waiving the participant business unit usage fee, according to the CSRC. The measures waiving listing fees for listed companies and bond transaction handling fees, which were already implemented earlier this year, will be extended for two years to 2028.
The Shenzhen Stock Exchange on the same day began soliciting public opinion on the market-making rules for stocks on the ChiNext board, China's Nasdaq-style board of growth enterprises.
The introduction of the market-maker system for the board is an important institutional arrangement to bolster market-support forces, strengthen market resilience and improve the quality of operations, according to the exchange.
The measures came after China's major stock indices moved lower in recent days, while U.S. stocks plunged on Friday, unsettling investors.
Earlier this month, China's central bank stepped up monetary policy support for the capital market, conducting the third operation of the Securities, Funds and Insurance companies Swap Facility to help financial institutions secure funding and boost their capacity to buy stocks, and reducing the interest rate of a relending facility for share buybacks and shareholding increases.

item.title: China urges U.S. to revoke proposed telecom restrictions: commerce ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
BEIJING, Nov. 22 (Xinhua) -- China on Sunday called on the United States to revoke proposed restrictions on Chinese telecom operators' direct access to U.S. phone numbers, saying the move violates the principles of non-discrimination and fair competition.
The U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) abused its regulatory powers and overstretched the concept of national security, while making arbitrary accusations against Chinese telecom companies without factual basis and maliciously undermining their operations in the United States, a commerce ministry spokesperson noted in response to a media query.
The FCC has recently continued to push to decouple and sever supply chains between China and the United States in telecommunications, communications, testing and certification, the spokesperson added.
Such moves run counter to the important consensus reached by the two heads of state and undermine the stability of China-U.S. economic and trade relations, the spokesperson said.
China urges the United States to immediately rescind the measures and return to the right way of resolving issues through consultations, the spokesperson said, noting that China will take necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own interests.

item.title: Chinese vice premier says China ready to strengthen AI, green development cooperation with Singapore
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
China is willing to work with Singapore to fully utilize the bilateral cooperation mechanism and deepen mutually beneficial cooperation in areas such as artificial intelligence (AI) and green development, Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang said on Sunday.
Ding, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks while meeting Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in Singapore. He is in Singapore to co-chair bilateral cooperation mechanism meetings with Singaporean Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong.
Ding congratulated Wong on his successful visit to China and attendance at the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, and noted that under the care and guidance of leaders from both countries, the China-Singapore bilateral cooperation mechanism meetings have continuously enriched their dimensions and yielded new achievements, laying a solid foundation for the all-round high-quality future-oriented partnership.
The two countries should sustain the sound momentum of close exchanges in education, science and technology, culture and other fields, so as to continuously consolidate the public foundation for the growth of bilateral relations, Ding said.
Wong expressed the belief that the mechanism meetings will consolidate and expand all-round cooperation between the two sides.
Wong said Singapore looks forward to strengthening cooperation with China in AI, the digital economy and other sectors, adding that the two sides should also further enhance people-to-people exchanges to boost mutual understanding.
As Singapore will assume the rotating chairmanship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) next year, it is ready to take this opportunity to advance ASEAN-China cooperation across various fields, Wong said.

item.title: Xi Story: Bringing Hainan's rainforest back to life
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
HAIKOU, Nov. 22 (Xinhua) -- Zhou Zhaoli, a member of the Hainan gibbon monitoring team, starts his day at 4:30 a.m., long before sunrise.
With flashlights in hand, he and his teammates pick their way through dense undergrowth in the mountainous Bawangling area of south China's Hainan Province, braving thorns and leech bites.
Their reward is sometimes the sight of Hainan gibbons high in the forest canopy, and the sound of their distinctive calls echoing through the trees at first light.
The world's 20 gibbon species live in 11 Asian countries, and most are in decline. Native to the island province's tropical rainforests, the Hainan gibbon was once pushed to the brink of extinction by commercial logging, deforestation and poaching. Today it is the only gibbon species in the world whose population has kept growing.
During an inspection tour of Hainan in April 2022, Chinese President Xi Jinping visited part of these rainforests and asked local villagers whether they had seen the rare primates. At that time, the habitat hosted 36 gibbons in five groups.
By the end of 2025, the figure reached 44 gibbons in seven groups, up from fewer than 10 in two groups in the early 1980s.
Hainan's tropical rainforest is China's largest, best-preserved and most concentrated stretch of contiguous island-type tropical rainforest.
The rainforest was once fragmented across more than 20 nature reserves and other protected areas in nine cities and counties. In 2019, Hainan began piloting an integrated approach, placing previously separate nature reserves, forest parks and state-owned forest farms under unified management.
About two years later, the Hainan Tropical Rainforest National Park was established as one of China's first five national parks, which together span ecosystems from giant panda habitats in Sichuan, Gansu and Shaanxi provinces to the only home of the Hainan gibbon.
Xi has closely followed the park's development. In 2018, he called for establishing national parks, including those protecting tropical rainforests. In 2019, he chaired a key reform meeting that approved a pilot plan for the Hainan national park. In 2021, he announced the establishment of China's first five national parks at the COP15 leaders' summit.
During that 2022 inspection tour, Xi walked along a boardwalk in the national park, taking a close look at its natural environment.
"He slowed his pace, studying the trees and listening closely to the sounds of nature as we walked," said Zheng Yan, a member of the park's public education and outreach team, who accompanied Xi and introduced the park to him during the visit.
The park has improved markedly in both infrastructure and management capacity since its establishment, said Zheng, who has worked there for more than a decade.
Xi's interest in rainforest conservation extends beyond China. On a visit to Brazil in July 2014, he recalled his 2009 trip to Manaus, a city deep in the Amazon rainforest, saying that protecting this vast expanse of pristine forest was vital to the global ecosystem.
Protecting tropical rainforests is closely tied to humanity's survival and well-being, and it is a shared responsibility that calls for concerted global efforts.
In recent years, China and Brazil have deepened cooperation on climate change and sustainable development. With support from the international community, the two countries are exploring new approaches to rainforest conservation and development, including measures that help local farmers improve their livelihoods and reduce deforestation while safeguarding the world's precious ecological assets and advancing global climate goals.
Greice Quele Aparecida Barboza de Oliveira, an environmental analyst with Brazil's Chico Mendes Institute for Biodiversity Conservation, visited Hainan recently to learn about China's approach to biodiversity conservation and to see how the national park protects the rare primate.
"These are areas I knew little about before. I am studying them closely so that I can take China's experience in wildlife conservation home with me," she said.
She was in Hainan for the 2026 Tropical Rainforest Ecosystem Partners Conference, which ended on Sunday and drew international officials, experts and representatives from more than 20 countries.
Climate change is becoming an increasingly serious challenge in Brazil and around the world, she said, adding that international cooperation and exchanges like those at the Hainan conference can help share effective conservation practices with other countries.
During his 2022 visit to Hainan, Xi also asked about forest rangers' income and village-level public spending. He stressed the need to strictly protect tropical rainforests while ensuring that ecological conservation, green development and improvements in people's livelihoods go hand in hand.
Hainan's tropical rainforest lies in one of the world's 34 biodiversity hotspots and serves as a reservoir of water, a source of food and wealth and a carbon sink.
"Hainan's tropical rainforest does not belong to Hainan alone. It belongs to the people of the whole country and to Mother Earth as a whole. It is a national treasure," Xi said.

item.title: China's tech innovation engine powers a connected Asia-Pacific
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
An APEC-themed installation is seen on Xiangmihu road in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 15, 2026. (Xinhua/Jin Liwang)
* China's push to unleash the potential of innovation and share technological dividends through open regional integration has resonated widely -- translating its innovation capacity into broader market opportunities and lending fresh momentum to economic growth and the building of an Asia-Pacific community.
* Across the Asia-Pacific, China's technological innovations are finding applications in a growing range of industries and aspects of everyday life.
* The release of the Shenzhen Initiative marked a milestone in the 30-year history of the APEC CEO Summit. It was a historic moment in Shenzhen, a city that has stood at the forefront of China's opening-up and has grown into a global innovation hub.
BEIJING, Nov. 22 (Xinhua) -- As host of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China has placed openness, innovation and cooperation at the heart of its agenda as the three priority areas. Throughout this week's sessions, participants explored how the Asia-Pacific can navigate structural shifts and cultivate new engines of economic growth.
INNOVATION THAT BENEFITS ALL
At an experimental durian orchard at Chiang Mai University in Thailand, agricultural lecturer Supakorn Wongsuk prepares a drone for takeoff. Having studied in China, he now applies the technology to explore more efficient methods of cultivating tropical fruits.
Lifting smoothly into the air, the drone glides above rows of durian trees, releasing a fine mist of pesticide across their leaves and branches.
"Using drones to spray pesticides can improve operational efficiency, reduce farmers' direct exposure to chemicals, and protect their health and safety," said Supakorn.
He sees the Chinese innovations as offering benefits that extend well beyond farming efficiency. "For young people, drone operations can also create new job opportunities."
The role of innovation also drew sharp focus at the APEC CEO Summit 2026 in Shenzhen.
"Innovation is very important, and innovation cannot be done overnight. It requires strong education support and accumulated experience. This is where we think China can play a role," said Indonesian Chamber of Commerce and Industry Chairman Anindya N. Bakrie.
"China has an important role to play," said Julien Leclair-Dionne, associate director at the University of Ottawa's Professional Development Institute. "Particularly given its technological capabilities, innovation ecosystem and experience in scaling emerging technologies."
An AI trainer operates a robot to collect data at a humanoid robot innovation center in Wuhan, central China's Hubei Province, Nov. 11, 2026. (Xinhua/Wu Zhizun)
"Ultimately, what matters most is not simply how advanced the technologies become, but how effectively the innovations are translated into opportunities for people, organizations and communities across the region," he said.
OPENNESS CREATES OPPORTUNITIES
Released on Wednesday, the Shenzhen Initiative of the APEC CEO Summit 2026 highlighted the transformative potential of frontier technologies such as artificial intelligence, while recognizing the accompanying risks and regulatory challenges that require coordinated regional oversight.
At the heart of the document lies a clear, unified conviction among business leaders: no single economy can capture the promise of breakthrough technology -- or tame its disruptions -- alone; only deep regional cooperation can turn innovation into shared prosperity.
Auckland Business Chamber CEO Simon Bridges emphasized the need for cooperation amid global uncertainty. "I think cooperation is probably the byword of APEC. And we know in the world right now, it's more important than ever," he said.
China's approach to AI development provides "a very good example" that allows others to learn from its technological advances, he added.
The appeal of Chinese AI models has become increasingly evident across the region. In South Korea, nearly half of the AI models released by local developers on Hugging Face, a globally popular open-source platform, between January and August this year were based on Chinese foundation models.
"China has adopted AI with more open-weight, open-source, low-cost models that are going to be used by businesses around the world," said Jacob Cooke, CEO of WPIC Marketing + Technologies, a leading e-commerce and technology consultancy.
"These Chinese companies have done their best to get this technology out to help people," Cooke said at the summit.
The opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 is held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi)
For Lee Ju-kwan, director of the National Center for APEC Studies at the Korea Institute for International Economic Policy of South Korea, Shenzhen's relentless innovation engine came vividly into focus during a visit to electric vehicle giant BYD's headquarters, offering a firsthand look at the homegrown tech muscle powering the city.
"I was deeply impressed by what I saw, particularly robots performing tasks that would traditionally be carried out by human workers on the production line," Lee said.
"This year, by hosting APEC, China has taken the opportunity to put forward and renew initiatives aimed at promoting openness and cooperation. I believe these efforts deserve attention and support," Lee said.
GREEN INNOVATION
"It's the most fantastic ride," said Jeffrey Sachs, a professor at Columbia University, looking back on an epic 15,000-km summer odyssey from Rome to China's Hong Kong, retracing Marco Polo's historic path behind the wheel of a BYD electric vehicle.
This photo taken on Sept. 9, 2026 shows an assembly line at the BYD Fuzhou base in Fuzhou, east China's Jiangxi Province. (Xinhua/Wan Xiang)
Sachs said the journey showed how far green technology had advanced. "The technology is already here. Most of it is in its most advanced stage in China," Sachs said during a high-level panel at the APEC CEO Summit 2026.
He also noted that China had significantly reduced the cost of green technologies, making the transition more affordable. "To go green is not to make an extra burden for the sake of the planet. It's just to have a low-cost, resilient, state-of-the-art energy system," he said.
The benefits of China's green innovation are also being felt by residents of Goulburn in New South Wales, Australia. With an integrated solar-and-storage solution supplied by a Chinese company, the local community has brought its own solar farm into operation.
The facility began supplying electricity to the grid in March, with part of its annual profits to be channeled into a community fund to help residents facing energy poverty.
"For a long time, it has been talk around the kitchen table. Suddenly here we are in amongst the panels, watching the sun send electrons to the people and my kids all own little parts of this with the community," said Goulburn resident Dave Suttle.
"Without China's involvement, we definitely wouldn't have solar cells as cheap as now," Martin Green, Scientia Professor of Photovoltaic and Renewable Energy Engineering at the University of New South Wales, told Xinhua.
Having worked with China's photovoltaic industry for more than four decades, Green is now collaborating with Chinese partners on the next generation of solar technology.
"Working with China, we feel we're in a position to improve the solar performance more quickly," he said.

item.title: Launch site ready for China's Shenzhou-24 spaceflight mission
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-22
This photo taken on Nov. 17, 2026 shows the combination of the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft and a Long March-2F carrier rocket being transferred to the launch area. (Photo by Ge Lixin/Xinhua)
JIUQUAN, Nov. 21 (Xinhua) -- The launch site for China's Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceflight mission has completed all preparations, with equipment, personnel and systems ready.
The Shenzhou-24 mission completed its final full-system joint rehearsal on Saturday, marking the last such exercise before liftoff. The rocket, spacecraft and all systems of the launch site are in good condition, according to the launch site.
Functional checks, joint tests and propellant loading will proceed as scheduled ahead of the launch.
On Nov. 17, the combination of the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft and its Long March-2F carrier rocket was transferred to the launch area.

item.title: Guarding green rainforest in China's southernmost province
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-22
A drone photo taken on Sept. 10, 2026 shows a view of the Wuzhishan section of the Hainan Tropical Rainforest National Park in south China's Hainan Province. (Xinhua/Pu Xiaoxu)
HAIKOU, Nov. 21 (Xinhua) -- Early in the morning, the mountainous rainforest of Wuzhishan in south China's Hainan Province is still shrouded in thick clouds and mist.
Wang Cheng opens the "Rainforest Patrol" application on his phone, gets on his motorcycle and sets off for his patrol mission through the mountains. As he travels, his route is automatically recorded on an electronic map.
Wang's family has lived at the foot of these mountains for generations, and the 44-year-old ethnic Li forest ranger treats the forests of his hometown as old friends, deserving of constant care and protection.
Decades ago, local villagers depended heavily on the mountains for their livelihoods. Logging and slash-and-burn farming had fragmented parts of the rainforest.
In 2021, China established its first five national parks, including the National Park of Hainan Tropical Rainforest. Since then, protecting the rainforest has become a shared responsibility, extending beyond the work of government departments and researchers to local communities. Many villagers inside the park have transitioned into forest ranger roles, with Wang being one of them.
This photo taken on Sept. 9, 2026 shows a stream at the Diaoluoshan section of the Hainan Tropical Rainforest National Park in south China's Hainan Province. (Xinhua/Pu Xiaoxu)
The transformation of Hainan's rainforest is once again in the international spotlight as the province hosts the ongoing 2026 Tropical Rainforest Ecosystem Partners Conference. The event, underway in the provincial capital Haikou, has brought together international officials, experts and representatives from more than 20 countries to exchange views on rainforest conservation and sustainable development.
Discussions have covered water conservation and ecological security, biodiversity protection, the development and utilization of forest food resources, mechanisms for realizing the value of ecological products, cultural heritage preservation and rainforest carbon governance.
International speakers at the conference highlighted the global importance of rainforest conservation, emphasizing its close links with food security, climate resilience and human well-being.
A think tank report titled "A Great Song Resounds in the Rainforest: The 'Hainan Model' of China's Tropical Rainforest Conservation" was released at the event, examining Hainan's experience in protecting its tropical rainforest ecosystem.
Hainan's tropical rainforest is the most concentrated, best-preserved and largest contiguous continental-island-type tropical rainforest in China, and forms an important part of the world's tropical rainforest system. Over the years, authorities have stepped up efforts to protect its valuable natural heritage.
The results are increasingly visible on the ground. On his patrols, Wang often spots tree crabs, which are indicators of a healthy rainforest ecosystem. Infrared cameras also frequently capture images of rare birds and animals.
Behind these observations is a "space-air-ground integrated" monitoring network operating within the park, combining satellite remote sensing, drones, acoustic monitoring devices and on-the-ground ranger patrols.
"When I see these creatures living and thriving peacefully, I know this forest has truly come back to life," Wang said.
The wildlife recovery reflects a whole set of systematic governance reforms. The National Park of Hainan Tropical Rainforest consolidated more than 20 previously scattered protected areas, relying on natural restoration supplemented by moderate artificial restoration to safeguard the rainforest's integrity.
The province has also completed China's first natural-resource ownership registration for a national park, taking stock of its forests, wetlands and water resources. Authorities orderly completed the ecological relocation of 459 households totaling 1,975 people from the core protected zone of the park.
Yet the challenges facing tropical rainforests extend far beyond Hainan.
The ongoing strong El Niño phenomenon is pushing the world's tropical rainforests to the brink of crisis. Rising forest fire risks, disturbed wildlife habitats and disrupted ecological water cycles continue to plague many tropical countries, where the tension between ecological protection and livelihood development persists.
"China's tropical rainforest management is already quite comprehensive," said Maria Rosda Lima Panggur, forest ecosystem manager at Komodo National Park in Indonesia, speaking at the conference.
The report not only profiles the biodiversity information, but also includes the cultural heritage -- how local communities relate to nature -- as well as conservation management and a big part of technology, such as smart patrols and monitoring, according to her.
"I think it's really a great effort for biodiversity conservation," she added.
For Wang, however, the challenges of rainforest conservation are increasingly apparent. El Niño has brought prolonged high temperatures and drought, adding to the daily pressure of forest management. During his patrols, he must now keep an even closer watch for fire risks and closely monitor the effects of dry weather on the survival of plants and animals.
"We guard the mountains, and the mountains guard us," he said.

item.title: Forum on overseas studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era held in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-22
Li Shulei, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and head of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, delivers a keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the 2026 edition of the International Forum on Overseas Studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 21, 2026. (Xinhua/Pang Xinglei)
BEIJING, Nov. 21 (Xinhua) -- The 2026 edition of the International Forum on Overseas Studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era opened in Beijing on Saturday.
Li Shulei, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and head of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, delivered a keynote speech at the opening ceremony.
Participants said Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era had taken shape and evolved through efforts to respond to questions posed by China, by the world, by the people, and by the times, and to advance China's development in tandem with that of the rest of the world.
They noted that Xi has proposed the vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity, offering China's answer to common challenges facing countries in the current era and has won broad recognition from the international community.
Participants called for stronger overseas research into and communication of the Thought, as well as joint efforts to advance global development, safeguard world peace and stability, promote human progress and improve the global governance system.
Under the theme "The Great Way: Building a Community with a Shared Future for Humanity," the forum was hosted by the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.
It will run through Sunday, with thematic sessions also being held in Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and five countries, namely Uzbekistan, Ethiopia, Greece, Hungary and Uruguay, bringing together nearly 650 participants from more than 80 countries and regions.
